ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a single-loop circuit, with a current source on the left, an adjacent arrow pointing upward and labeled Is; a resistor R is connected in series above; on the right is a voltage source U, with polarity marked as "+" at the upper end and "-" at the lower end. Then reason: From the arrow of the current source on the left, it can be known that the loop current is Is = 1 A, in the clockwise direction, so the current direction through the voltage source on the right is from top to bottom. This current enters the positive terminal of the voltage source, so according to the passive sign convention, the voltage source absorbs power. The power p_U = U × Is = 2 V × 1 A = 2 W.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: a one-loop circuit with the current source forcing clockwise current, a top resistor, and a right voltage source whose top node is positive. The series current is I = I_S = 1 A. The resistor absorbs I^2R = 1^2 × 2 = 2 W and has a 2 V drop in the current direction. The right voltage source has U = 2 V with current entering its positive terminal, so KVL implies the current source must supply the total voltage rise of 4 V and hence 4 W. By power balance, the two passive absorptions must sum to 4 W; after the resistor’s 2 W, the voltage source absorbs 2 W.
